title: SDK transport examples + keep-alive, pooling, and retry patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create cross-SDK (Python, TypeScript, Go) guidance and example snippets for recommended transport configuration: connection pooling, keep-alive tuning, timeouts, and retry patterns. This ticket bundles reference sample code, recommended defaults for hosted usage, and streaming ergonomics guidance to reduce common customer errors (stale connections, head-of-line blocking, inappropriate timeout windows). The goal is a single reference doc + example repo that SDKs link to and platform docs reference.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical guidance doc exists with per-language examples and rationale.
- Examples include: connection pool sizing, idle/keepalive timeouts, handshake/read/write deadlines, and safe retry/backoff strategies.
- Streaming section contains an example of graceful reconnect and resume semantics and advice on per-chunk vs overall deadlines.
- SDKs (python/ts/go) have linked PRs that reference the examples and implement the recommended defaults or helper utilities.
- Benchmarks or smoke tests (simple curl/bench harness) show reduced connection churn in a simulated long-lived workload.
- Docs reviewed by runtime and SDK owners and approved in PRs.
decisions:
- Default client should expose a reusable transport/agent; do not create new TCP connections per request.
- Keep default max idle connections conservative for hosted: 64 per host; document raising for Dedicated.
- Expose sane timeout defaults but allow overrides per-request.
- SDKs will provide helper retry utilities but require callers to opt-in for non-idempotent operations.
- Streaming endpoints will default to a short initial token timeout and a longer idle-chunk timeout; explicit resume API recommended for robust resume behavior.
